dimensions.intent: What the user is trying to do: execute, navigate, choose, disclose, inspect, or understand.
dimensions.apply: When the choice takes effect: immediate, submit, navigation, or none.
dimensions.scope: What the control affects: row, section, page, global, form, or marketing.
dimensions.space: Whether the context is compact or regular.
dimensions.content: Whether labels are plain, descriptive, searchable, grouped, rich, or tabular.
dimensions.risk: Whether the action is normal or destructive.
dimensions.optionCount: How many choices or actions are present.
dimensions.frequency: How often the action appears or is used: repeated, routine, occasional, or rare.
dimensions.importance: Its local hierarchy: principal, supporting, quiet, or destructive.
dimensions.expressiveness: Whether the visual direction calls for restrained, standard, or expressive treatment.

useWhen: A visible label triggers one action in the current context.
The action needs primary, supporting, quiet, or destructive emphasis.
avoidWhen: The destination has a URL.
The control is an icon-only repeated utility.
Several actions need a shared container.

useWhen: Two or three closely related actions should remain visible together.
avoidWhen: The control represents one selected value.
More than three actions can be grouped in a menu.
Actions are unrelated but merely adjacent.

useWhen: A familiar icon performs a compact utility action.
A row, toolbar, or header needs an icon-dominant trigger with an accessible name and usually a tooltip.
avoidWhen: The action label carries important meaning.
The icon is unfamiliar.
The control is the main call to action.

useWhen: A rare, high-attention marketing or milestone action earns decorative emphasis.
avoidWhen: The surface is a dense product UI.
The action repeats in rows or cards.
Decoration would compete with task hierarchy.

useWhen: The interaction navigates to a real destination but needs button-like prominence.
avoidWhen: The interaction mutates data or opens a local UI.
A normal text link provides sufficient emphasis.

useWhen: Representing one person, organization, or account.
avoidWhen: Showing a generic feature icon.
Representing several overlapping identities.

useWhen: Several people or organizations should remain individually recognizable.
avoidWhen: Only one identity exists.
Space is too narrow for the full group.

useWhen: A constrained row or toolbar needs a compact summary of several identities.
avoidWhen: Individual identities and labels must all remain visible.
Only one identity exists.

useWhen: Showing compact, non-interactive category, type, count, or metadata.
avoidWhen: Communicating operational state.
Representing a removable selection.
Showing a page-level message.

useWhen: Persistent information applies to most or all of a page.
avoidWhen: Feedback is local to a field or section.
The message is a transient confirmation.
The message needs an interruptive decision.

useWhen: Users must compare repeated records across shared columns.
Sorting, selection, row actions, or bulk actions follow a clear reading model.
avoidWhen: Items have unrelated schemas.
The content is better scanned as a simple list.
The mobile transformation has not been planned.

useWhen: A subtle boundary clarifies grouping after spacing alone has been considered.
avoidWhen: A larger gap or heading already expresses the relationship.
Repeated dividers create visual noise.

useWhen: Displaying a real keyboard key or shortcut.
avoidWhen: Displaying an ordinary label, status, or decorative glyph.

useWhen: Showing determinate completion or a value against a known linear maximum.
Horizontal space supports a labeled comparison.
avoidWhen: The value is indeterminate.
A compact radial footprint is required.
The value is merely decorative.

useWhen: Determinate progress needs a compact radial footprint or centered value.
avoidWhen: Precise comparison across several rows matters.
A horizontal bar would communicate scale more clearly.

useWhen: Showing or collecting an ordered rating on a familiar fixed scale.
avoidWhen: The value is status, progress, or an arbitrary score without a familiar scale.

useWhen: Showing operational, lifecycle, validation, or process state.
avoidWhen: The value is merely a category.
The item is removable or selected.

useWhen: Representing a selected, removable, or manipulable entity or filter token.
avoidWhen: Showing static classification or operational status.

useWhen: Feedback belongs persistently within the affected flow or section.
The user may need to act on the message in context.
avoidWhen: The message applies to the whole page.
The message is a brief confirmation after an action.

useWhen: A richer message includes source, time, description, or actions and may persist in a notification center.
avoidWhen: A short transient confirmation is enough.
The message must block progress.

useWhen: Confirming a completed, non-blocking action without moving focus.
avoidWhen: The information must remain available.
The user must act before continuing.
The error needs field-level correction.

useWhen: Providing a short accessible label or clarification for a focused or hovered control.
avoidWhen: The information is required to complete the task.
The content is interactive or long.
The trigger is not focusable.

useWhen: Selecting zero, one, or many independent options.
A binary form value takes effect on submit.
avoidWhen: Exactly one choice is required from a group.
A setting should apply immediately.

useWhen: The user must choose or enter a color and needs visual color feedback.
avoidWhen: Only a few named theme choices exist; use visible choices instead.
Color is decorative rather than user-controlled data.

useWhen: Choosing a date benefits from calendar context, range constraints, or nearby-date comparison.
avoidWhen: A known date is faster to type.
Only month, year, or relative period selection is required.

useWhen: Entering a short fixed-length verification or access code one digit at a time.
avoidWhen: Entering arbitrary numbers, money, phone numbers, or long identifiers.

useWhen: Selecting or dropping one or more files with type, size, progress, and error feedback.
avoidWhen: The task selects an existing remote asset.
A simple URL input is required.

useWhen: Persistent concise guidance, constraints, or validation context belongs to a field.
avoidWhen: The information is optional hover help.
The message is page-level feedback.

useWhen: Entering or editing one line of text, search, email, number, or similarly compact data.
avoidWhen: The value spans multiple lines.
The value comes from a controlled option set.
A specialized date, file, color, or code control exists.

useWhen: Giving a persistent accessible name to a form control or group.
avoidWhen: Using helper text as a substitute for a name.
The text is a heading rather than a field label.

useWhen: Choosing exactly one option from a short list.
Seeing all choices or comparing descriptions matters before submission.
avoidWhen: Choices apply immediately as a view or mode switch.
Space cannot support visible choices.
Multiple selections are allowed.

useWhen: Choosing one value from a moderate predefined list.
A compact toolbar or form cannot keep all options visible.
avoidWhen: A short list should remain visible for comparison.
The list is long enough to require search.
Several options may be selected.

useWhen: Adjusting an approximate value within a known range with immediate visual feedback.
avoidWhen: Exact numeric entry is required.
The range or current value is unknown.
Only two states exist.

useWhen: Turning one persistent setting on or off with immediate effect.
avoidWhen: The value is submitted with a form.
The user chooses among more than two options.
The action is one-time rather than a setting.

useWhen: Entering or editing content that may wrap across several lines.
avoidWhen: The expected answer is one short line.
Structured choices can replace free-form text.

useWhen: Several related sections can be independently expanded to reduce initial complexity.
avoidWhen: All information is required simultaneously.
The sections are peer views or navigation destinations.

useWhen: Showing the current location within a genuine multi-level hierarchy.
avoidWhen: The product has a flat information architecture.
The sequence represents progress rather than location.

useWhen: Two to five closely related modes, formats, ranges, or filters apply immediately.
Short labels can remain visible in one line.
avoidWhen: The choice belongs to a submitted form.
Options need descriptions.
The items are independent actions or separate information sections.

useWhen: Switching among a small number of equal-importance peer sections in the same context.
avoidWhen: The control only changes a view format or filter.
Labels cannot fit without excessive truncation.
The content levels have unequal importance.

useWhen: Peer sections need longer labels, counts, icons, or a persistent vertical rail.
avoidWhen: Horizontal space is scarce.
The hierarchy is nested navigation rather than peer sections.

useWhen: Compact progress through a short sequence matters more than step labels.
avoidWhen: Users need step names, status details, or non-linear navigation.

useWhen: A short ordered process needs visible step labels across a wide layout.
avoidWhen: Labels are long, steps are numerous, or narrow layouts dominate.
The sequence is hierarchical location.

useWhen: A long collection is split into stable pages and users may jump or move sequentially.
avoidWhen: Continuous loading or a small complete collection is more appropriate.
The sequence represents workflow steps.

useWhen: A longer ordered process needs labels, descriptions, status, or nested content.
avoidWhen: Only compact progress is required.
The items are independent sections.

useWhen: Searching and invoking commands or destinations across a large, grouped set.
Keyboard-first discovery is valuable.
avoidWhen: A short value list fits a select or radio group.
The content is explanatory rather than actionable.

useWhen: A substantial secondary workflow or detail view should preserve page context.
Mobile navigation or filters need a temporary side surface.
avoidWhen: A short bounded decision fits a modal.
Only a few actions or a small explanation are needed.

useWhen: A trigger reveals a compact list of immediate actions.
Overflow actions belong to a row, card, toolbar, or page header.
avoidWhen: The user is choosing a form value.
The overlay contains substantial explanatory or interactive content.
One action should remain directly visible.

useWhen: A focused decision or bounded task must be completed or dismissed before returning.
A destructive or consequential action needs confirmation and context.
avoidWhen: The task can remain inline.
The workflow is long or benefits from page context.
The content is merely informative.

useWhen: Compact contextual information or a small interactive control belongs near its trigger.
avoidWhen: The content is only a short label.
The content is a menu of immediate actions.
Focus must be trapped for a consequential decision.
